evidence: src/infrastructure/composition/Dependencies.ts: `export interface Dependencies { users: UserRepository; projects: ProjectRepository; tasks: TaskRepository; ids: IdGenerator; }`: the one shared abstraction for the adapters.

src/infrastructure/composition/AppFactory.ts: `createApp()` is the only place that creates `new InMemoryUserRepository()`, `new InMemoryProjectRepository()`, `new InMemoryTaskRepository()` and `new UuidIdGenerator()`, then passes `deps` to every feature module.
src/infrastructure/composition/ProjectModule.ts: `createProjectRoutes(deps: Dependencies)` wires CreateProjectUseCase, CreateTaskUseCase and ListProjectTasksUseCase from `deps` only.
src/infrastructure/composition/TaskModule.ts: `createTaskRoutes(deps: Dependencies)` wires AssignTaskUseCase and CompleteTaskUseCase from `deps.tasks` and `deps.users` only.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This module passes. It is the app's composition root (the place where the app is wired together), and all five files share that one concern. Dependencies.ts defines a single `Dependencies` interface that lists the shared adapters as their domain/application port types. AppFactory.ts is the only file that creates concrete adapters (InMemory*Repository, UuidIdGenerator). It builds them once and passes the same `deps` object to each feature module. Each feature module (UserModule, ProjectModule, TaskModule) receives only `Dependencies` and builds its own use cases and controller, returning a Router. No file creates its own adapter instance or skips the `Dependencies` abstraction. Adapter creation happens only in AppFactory, and the shape of the shared adapter set is defined only in Dependencies.ts, so no rule is duplicated. CreateTaskUseCase is wired in ProjectModule rather than TaskModule. That is a reasonable choice because creating a task is a project-scoped route on ProjectController, and the use case is not wired anywhere else, so nothing is duplicated.
